routes.name: Short stay without a visa (Schengen, 90 days in 180)
routes.summary: Citizens of countries not on the Schengen visa-required list can visit France for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Entries and exits are now logged in the Entry/Exit System (EES).

other: Applies to nationalities that do not need a Schengen visa. I could not open the official country list, so check your passport on the France-Visas site.
No work allowed.
EES biometrics (face and, from age 12, fingerprints) are collected at the border. EES was due to be fully operational on 10 April 2026.

sources.label: French Ministry of Foreign Affairs: EES

routes.name: ETIAS travel authorization
routes.summary: A small online travel authorization for visa-exempt nationals. The foreign ministry page said it was expected to go live in the last quarter of 2026, so confirm it is running before you travel.

other: For nationals who can enter the Schengen area without a visa.
Not confirmed as operational as of the page I read. Check the current status.

routes.processing: Decision typically within 96 hours, per the foreign ministry page.

sources.label: French Ministry of Foreign Affairs: EES and ETIAS

routes.name: Short-stay visa for a business trip
routes.summary: A Schengen short-stay visa for trade fairs, seminars, conferences and similar work visits. The stay cannot go over 90 days.

other: You need a clear link between your job and the trip.
Only for nationalities that need a visa. Others can use the visa-free rule.

steps: Use the France-Visas wizard to confirm what you need.
Fill in the online application.
Book an appointment at the consulate or visa center.
File your documents and collect your passport.
documents: Invitation or request letter from your French contact describing the activity, purpose, duration and place
If no letter: admission cards for the fair or conference
If neither: a commitment from the host company to cover all your costs

routes.name: Visitor residence permit (carte de sejour visiteur)
routes.summary: For non-EU people who want to live in France for more than 3 months without working. You need enough money for the whole stay and health insurance. Valid up to one year.

income.note: About 1,477.93 EUR net per month for a single person. Family allowances do not count and housing costs are weighed.

other: Health insurance covering the stay.
You cannot work in France in any form.
Not for EU/EEA/Swiss citizens (they have their own rules) or Algerians (separate certificate).

steps: Apply for a long-stay visa at the French consulate or visa center in your country.
Validate it after arrival, or apply for the card, as your visa instructs.
Renew online 4 to 2 months before expiry.

fees.label: Residence card (first issue)
fees.note: 300 EUR tax plus 50 EUR stamp duty

fees.label: Late filing penalty
fees.note: Unless force majeure or you hold a valid visa

routes.name: Talent Passport: Qualified employee of an innovative company
routes.summary: A multi-year permit for a qualified employee of an innovative company working on its R&D project. Up to 4 years.

other: Employment contract of more than 3 months.
Salary of at least 2 times the minimum legal wage (full time).
Employer must prove it is an innovative company for tax purposes.

stay.note: Matches the contract, max 4 years. Under 12 months you get a long-stay visa that works as a residence permit (validate within 3 months).

documents: Proof of the company's innovative status

routes.name: Talent Passport: Intra-company transferee (employee on mission)
routes.summary: For employees sent from a foreign group company to a French group company. Up to 4 years.

other: At least 3 months with the group company abroad.
French contract of more than 3 months.
Salary of at least 1.8 times the minimum legal wage.

routes.name: Talent Passport: Researcher
routes.summary: For researchers or higher-education staff hosted by an approved institution. Up to 4 years. A separate 'researcher mobility' version exists for EU or multilateral programs.

other: Hosting agreement with an approved institution.
No salary threshold stated on the page.

documents: Hosting agreement with an approved institution

routes.name: Talent Passport: EU Blue Card
routes.summary: For highly qualified workers with a job offer of at least one year and a salary of at least 1.5 times the average gross reference salary. Up to 4 years.

income.note: 1.5 times the average gross reference salary, as set on 21 August 2025

eligibility.education: 3 years of higher education, or 5 years of comparable experience
other: Contract of at least one year.

routes.name: Talent Passport: Business creator
routes.summary: For people starting a real commercial, craft or industrial business in France. You need a Master's level or 5 years of experience and at least 30,000 EUR of personal investment. Up to 4 years.

eligibility.education: Master's level, or 5 years of professional experience
other: The business project must be real and serious.

routes.name: Talent Passport: Economic investor
routes.summary: For investors who take a lasting interest in a French company, for example over 10 percent equity, real estate, capital increase or reinvested earnings. No minimum amount is stated on the page. Up to 4 years.

other: Investment must give a lasting interest in the company.
No minimum amount stated on the official page.

routes.name: Talent Passport: Innovative economic project
routes.summary: For founders whose project has been recognized beforehand by a public body. You must show means of living at least equal to the minimum legal wage. Up to 4 years.

other: Project recognized beforehand by a public body.
Means of subsistence at least equal to the minimum legal wage.

routes.name: Talent Passport: Company representative (mandataire social)
routes.summary: For senior people in a group company abroad who become legal representative of a French entity. Pay must be at least 3 times the minimum legal wage. Up to 4 years.

other: At least 3 months as an employee or officer in a group entity.
Mandate to act as legal representative in France.
Pay of at least 3 times the minimum legal wage.

routes.name: Talent Passport: National or international reputation
routes.summary: For people with a name in science, literature, the arts, academia, education or sports who plan to stay more than 3 months. Up to 4 years.

other: Proven reputation in your field.
Means of subsistence at least equal to the minimum legal wage.
Stay of more than 3 months.

documents: Nature, purpose and length of your project

routes.name: Talent Passport: Performer or creator of a literary or artistic work
routes.summary: For performers and creators with an engagement of at least 3 months in France. Up to 4 years depending on contracts.

other: Performance or production engagement of at least 3 months.
Resources of at least 70 percent of the monthly minimum legal wage. Your own resources can cover up to 49 percent of the total. Unemployment benefits do not count.

stay.note: Based on engagements and contracts, max 4 years.

routes.name: Employee or temporary worker residence permit (salarie / travailleur temporaire)
routes.summary: The general work route. Your employer gets a work authorization first. The first card lasts 1 year, then a 4-year multi-year card is possible.

other: Job must be on the shortage list, or advertised 3 weeks in the last 6 months with no valid applicants.
Salary at least the SMIC, or the collective agreement rate if higher.
Permanent contract (CDI) gives the 'salarie' card. Fixed-term (CDD) gives 'travailleur temporaire'.
A new work authorization is needed for each new contract.
Not for Algerians (separate rules).

stay.note: 1 year first, then a 4-year multi-year card if still employed and integration conditions are met.

steps: Employer applies online for the work authorization.
You apply for a long-stay visa marked 'salarie' or 'travailleur temporaire'.
Validate the visa online within 3 months of arrival.
Renew 2 months before it expires.

fees.label: Residence card, first issue
fees.note: 300 EUR tax plus 50 EUR stamp duty

fees.label: Visa validation fee when arriving on a long-stay visa
Employer tax, contract of 12 months or more
fees.note: Cap. Below a monthly gross of 4,667.54 EUR it is 55 percent of the monthly gross. Paid by the first employer.

sources.label: Service-Public: Work authorization for a foreign employee

routes.name: Seasonal worker permit (travailleur saisonnier)
routes.summary: For seasonal jobs, capped at 6 months of work per year. The seasonal contract must be the basis of the application.

other: Only a seasonal fixed-term contract lets you start directly. Other contracts need a long-stay visa from your home country.
Employer must prove you will have decent housing.
Salary at least the SMIC or the collective agreement rate.

stay.note: Seasonal work is limited to 6 months per year.

sources.label: Service-Public: Work authorization for a foreign employee

routes.name: Entrepreneur / liberal profession residence permit
routes.summary: For self-employed people, freelancers and business owners. The activity must be your main one and economically viable. First card is 1 year, then a 4-year card is possible.

other: Activity registered with the one-stop shop for company formalities.
New business: show it is economically viable (business plan).
Liberal profession or existing activity: show resources equal to the full-time minimum legal wage.
Regulated professions need the required diplomas.

stay.note: First card up to 1 year. Visa version must be validated within 15 days of arrival per France-Visas.

routes.name: Student long-stay visa and residence permit
routes.summary: For studying at a French higher-education school. The visa works as a residence permit for up to a year, then you renew. After a year you can get a multi-year student permit.

income.note: Not required if you passed the entrance exam of a school with a State agreement

other: Registered or pre-registered at a higher-education school.
Follow Parcoursup or Campus France enrolment rules where they apply.

stay.note: Visa is 4 months to 1 year. Card is 1 year, renewable. Multi-year permit covers the rest of the course.

steps: Get admitted to a school.
Apply through France-Visas and book a consulate appointment.
Validate the visa online within 3 months of arrival.
Renew online 4 to 2 months before the card expires.

fees.label: Visa application, countries on the EEF procedure

documents: Certificate of enrolment from the school
Temporary address for the first 3 months

sources.label: Service-Public: Student visa or residence permit

routes.name: Working holiday visa (vacances-travail)
routes.summary: A one-year long-stay visa for young people from 16 partner countries. The main purpose must be tourism and culture, with paid work only as a side activity.

other: Age limits by country: under 30 for Chile, Ecuador, Hong Kong, Mexico, Peru. Under 31 for Brazil, Colombia, South Korea, Japan, New Zealand, Russia, Taiwan, Uruguay. Under 36 for Argentina, Australia, Canada.
You must meet the funds and length rules in your country's agreement.

routes.name: Family of a French national (spouse, children, parents)
routes.summary: Spouses, children under 21, dependent older relatives and parents of a minor French child can get a long-stay visa and then a residence permit. Spouses get a visa that works as a residence permit.

other: Spouse of a French national, shared life must continue in France.
Child under 21 of a French parent, or older if dependent.
Parent or grandparent of a French national or their spouse, if dependent.
Parent of a minor French child who has supported the child since birth or for at least 2 years.

stay.note: Spouse visa works as a residence permit. Children, dependent relatives and parents get a 3-month visa, then apply at the prefecture.

routes.name: Family reunification (family of a foreign resident)
routes.summary: A legal resident can bring a spouse and minor children from abroad. The resident needs 18 months in France, enough income and suitable housing. Decision by the prefect within 6 months.

income.note: Gross SMIC, average over the prior 12 months, for a family of 2 or 3. 2,053.72 EUR for 4 or 5. 2,240.42 EUR for 6 or more.

other: Sponsor holds a card valid at least 1 year, a multi-year card or a resident card.
At least 18 months of residence on a qualifying permit.
Housing must meet minimum floor space by zone, for example 22 m2 for a couple in zones A bis and A.
Spouse must be 18 or older. Children must be under 18.
Parents of the resident are not covered, they can apply for visitor status.
Algerians follow separate rules.

steps: Check eligibility with the official simulator.
File online or by registered mail with OFII.
Mayor checks resources and housing within 2 months, then the prefect decides within 6 months.
Spouse applies for a long-stay visa and enters France within 3 months.
Validate the visa online and do the OFII medical exam. Sign the republican integration contract.

routes.name: Multi-year residence card (carte de sejour pluriannuelle)
routes.summary: Usually issued after a first year on a temporary card or visa. Generally valid 4 years. Since 1 January 2026 a first card needs A2 French and the civic exam, unless you are over 65.

other: Must still meet the conditions of your current permit.
Pass the civic exam (in force 1 January 2026, taken before the permit is issued).
Sign the commitment to the principles of the Republic.
You cannot get it on the same basis if you hold a visitor, au pair, intern or temporary worker card.
Student cards cover the rest of the course (up to 4 years). Some private and family life cards are max 2 years.

stay.note: Generally 4 years for employee and entrepreneur cards.

fees.label: Multi-year card (general case)
fees.note: 300 EUR tax plus 50 EUR stamp duty. 150 EUR for student cards.

routes.name: 10-year resident card (carte de resident)
routes.summary: A 10-year renewable card for certain categories, such as spouses of French nationals married 3 years, family reunification beneficiaries with 3 years in France, and refugees. Since 1 January 2026 it needs B1 French and the civic exam.

eligibility.language: CEFR B1 French (first card, under 65, some categories exempt)
other: Spouse of a French national: married at least 3 years with a shared life.
Family reunification spouse or child: at least 3 years of regular residence.
Parent of a French child: at least 3 years on a private and family life card.
Refugees get it directly. Stateless people and subsidiary protection holders need 4 years on a multi-year permit.
Pass the civic exam and show commitment to republican principles.
The card lapses after more than 3 consecutive years outside France.

fees.label: Resident card (most categories)
fees.note: 300 EUR tax plus 50 EUR stamp duty. Free for refugees. Entering without a long-stay visa adds 300 EUR.

routes.name: EU long-term resident card
routes.summary: A 10-year card for non-EU people with 5 years of legal, continuous residence in France. You need stable income, health insurance, B1 French and the civic exam.

income.note: Gross monthly SMIC. Most social benefits are excluded.

other: 5 years of legal, uninterrupted residence on eligible permits. Absences up to 6 consecutive months and 10 months total.
Blue Card holders: at least 2 years on the Blue Card plus 3 years of earlier regular residence in France or another EU country.
Health insurance.
Civic exam with the 'resident card' mention.
Over 65: judged on commitment to the Republic's principles, no language or exam requirement.

stay.note: Lapses after 6 consecutive years outside France, or more than 3 consecutive years outside the EU.

fees.label: First issue
fees.note: 250 EUR if you already hold a valid residence permit

routes.name: EU/EEA/Swiss free movement and residence
routes.summary: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens can stay in France up to 3 months with just a passport or ID. Longer stays are allowed with a job, studies, or enough money and health insurance. A residence card is optional. After 5 years you can get a permanent card.

income.note: For a retired or inactive single person with no children, applies to the stay beyond 3 months without working. 977.54 EUR for a couple. Rises with children.

other: Health insurance needed if you are inactive or retired.
Working and student rules for stays over 3 months were not read on the pages I opened.

stay.note: Up to 3 months with no formalities. Longer stays need to meet the conditions above.

fees.label: Residence card (optional)
fees.note: Free for retired or inactive EU citizens

sources.label: Service-Public: Retired or inactive EU/EEA/Swiss citizen
Service-Public: Visa for overseas trips (EU citizen rule)

routes.name: Asylum and international protection
routes.summary: Apply through a Spada and the prefecture, and Ofpra decides. Refugee status brings a 10-year resident card. Subsidiary protection brings a multi-year permit.

other: Procedures were being updated by recent decrees when the page was read. Check the current rules with the prefecture or Ofpra.

steps: Pre-register at a Spada in your region and get a Guda interview date.
Register with the prefecture and get your asylum seeker certificate.
Send your form to Ofpra within 21 days.
Ofpra decides. Appeals go to the CNDA within one month.

routes.name: Naturalization by decree
routes.summary: French citizenship after 5 years of residence, with B2 French and the civic exam. Rules tightened for 2026: B2 level set by Decree 2025-648 and new language orders of 22 December 2025, and a mandatory civic exam from 1 January 2026.

eligibility.language: CEFR B2 French, spoken and written
other: At least 5 years of residence in France, with some exceptions the page does not list.
Pass the civic exam before applying (digital, 40 questions, pass mark 32).
Assimilation interview at the prefecture.
Proof of French: a qualifying diploma, or a TCF or TEF certificate less than 2 years old.
Exemptions exist for certain medical conditions.

routes.processing: The administration has up to 18 months from your receipt to decide, or 12 months if you have lived in France 10 years or more. It can be extended once by 3 months.

citizenship.note: French law does not make you give up your other nationality. Check your other country's rules.

sources.label: Service-Public: Proving your French level for nationality

routes.name: French nationality by marriage
routes.summary: Declaration after 4 years of marriage to a French spouse (5 if you lived abroad part of the time and your spouse was not on the consular register). Needs B2 French and the civic exam.

other: Married 4 years with continuous shared life in France. 4 or 5 years if you spent part of the marriage abroad (depends on consular registration).
Spouse was French on the wedding day and stayed French.
Foreign marriages must be recorded in the French civil registry.
Valid residence permit when you file, unless EEA or Swiss.
No expulsion order and no serious criminal record.

citizenship.note: French law does not require giving up another nationality.

sources.label: Service-Public: Proving your French level for nationality

routes.name: French nationality by descent
routes.summary: A child is French at birth if at least one parent is French, in France or abroad, with legal filiation established. The page I read does not say how many generations back it applies.

other: At least one French parent with filiation legally established.
Generation limits for children born abroad were not on the pages I read. Check with the consulate.

sources.label: Service-Public: In what cases is a child French

routes.name: French nationality for children born in France to foreign parents
routes.summary: Automatic at 18 if you live in France and have lived there at least 5 years since age 11. You can also claim it by declaration from age 13 (with a parent) or 16 (yourself).

other: Born in France to foreign parents who are not diplomats or career consuls.
Age 13 to 15: lived in France at least 5 years since age 8, declaration by the legal representative.
Age 16 to 17: lived in France at least 5 years since age 11, declaration by you.
At 18: automatic with 5 years of habitual residence since age 11. You can get a certificate of nationality as proof.
Children born to a parent who was born in France, or born stateless in France, are French at birth.

sources.label: Service-Public: Child born in France to foreign parents
Service-Public: In what cases is a child French
